correctness.rationale: Full proof: the two-phase conjunction induction yields exact t-consecutive full-pair output windows for all t, including doubled edges. Circular start-position inclusion–exclusion gives A(n,t), with a necessary subtraction of the all-ones case. Component independence yields the product and persistence law. The factorial-moment proof establishes the discrete Poisson phase limit. Standalone direct simulation passed 87,380 initial subsets of connected components (669,924 window checks) and 6,736 initial subsets of disconnected examples; exhaustive colored-word counts also checked 28 n,t pairs. Finite tests are ancillary, not general proof.

value.rationale: This gives a complete exact stopping-time law for arbitrary two-perfect-matching granulations and sharply contrasts worst-case linear convergence with typical logarithmic disappearance on a long connected component. It is motivated by repeated information-approximation processes; the precise all-time probabilities, persistent-component distinction and phase-dependent limiting law were not supplied by identified prior two-step results. It is not a renaming of a standalone Bernoulli-run theorem: the operator-to-run identification and disconnected-frame product formula are proved as part of the claim.
